data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2019 was GBP 114.024m. Using the published gross claims development triangle, there is a calculated aggregate adverse prior-year development of approximately GBP 7.7m (6.8% of opening gross reserves), driven principally by adverse development on older accident years (notably up to 2017), with causes cited including natural catastrophe activity and US casualty inflationary pressures. The managing agent's narrative reports a net prior year deficit of GBP 1.8m (after reinsurance), indicating material offsetting reinsurance recoveries. Specific 2018 catastrophe events (Hawaii volcano, Hurricanes Florence and Michael, Californian wildfires) and 2017/2018 hurricane activity (Irma/Michael) are referenced as influencing reserve movements, while 2019 typhoons Faxai and Hagibis produced losses contained within expected catastrophe budgets.
raw_causal_phrases: US Casualty reserve deterioration arising from "social inflation"

The industry has certainly witnessed considerable deterioration since the early evaluation of certain losses arising from natural catastrophes, most notably Hurricanes Irma and Michael and Typhoon Jebi.
We are certainly not immune to the inflation of claims values in the US.
In 2019, there has been an overall deficit of GBP 1.8m on prior year reserves (2018:deficit GBP 9.0m).

data.data_quality_notes: The gross prior-year movement was calculated from the report's gross claims development triangle (cumulative gross claims incurred) as a fallback, because the movement line in the technical provisions table shows combined current-year movement. The managing agent's narrative reports a net prior-year deficit of GBP 1.8m (after reinsurance), which differs from the gross triangle-derived adverse movement (~GBP 7.7m) due to reinsurance recoveries. Some LOB-level reserve movements are inferred from narrative and are not quantified in the report.
